title: Seviyan Vermicelli

description: Seviyan Vermicelli is a beloved Pakistani sweet dish, often enjoyed during Eid and special occasions. This comforting dessert features delicate roasted vermicelli simmered in fragrant milk with sugar and aromatic spices. Garnished with nuts and dried fruits, it offers a delightful balance of creamy texture and sweet, nutty flavors.

instructions.title: Roast the Vermicelli
instructions.text: Heat ghee or butter in a heavy-bottomed pot or pan over medium-low heat. Add the broken vermicelli pieces and roast them, stirring continuously, until they turn light golden brown and become fragrant. Be careful not to burn them. Remove the roasted vermicelli and set aside.

instructions.title: Boil the Milk
instructions.text: In the same pot, add the full-fat milk and the lightly crushed green cardamom pods. Bring the milk to a gentle boil over medium heat, stirring occasionally to prevent it from sticking to the bottom.

instructions.title: Add Sugar and Vermicelli
instructions.text: Once the milk boils, reduce the heat to low. Add the granulated sugar and stir until it completely dissolves. Then, gently add the roasted vermicelli to the boiling milk.

instructions.title: Simmer and Thicken
instructions.text: Let the vermicelli simmer on low heat, stirring occasionally, until it softens and absorbs most of the milk, and the mixture thickens to a creamy consistency. This usually takes about 10-15 minutes. Add raisins if using.

instructions.title: Add Flavoring
instructions.text: Once the seviyan has reached the desired consistency, remove it from heat. If using, stir in the kewra water or rose water for an extra aromatic touch.

instructions.title: Garnish and Serve
instructions.text: Ladle the hot Seviyan Vermicelli into serving bowls. Garnish generously with sliced almonds and chopped pistachios. Serve warm or at room temperature. It can also be chilled and served cold.

tips: For a richer flavor, toast the vermicelli in ghee until golden brown; this step adds a distinct nutty aroma and prevents it from becoming mushy.
Always use full-fat milk for the creamiest texture. If you prefer a thinner consistency, you can add a little more milk towards the end of cooking.
Seviyan can be served warm, at room temperature, or chilled. Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2-3 days.
